MELBOURNE, Nov 28 : Veteran spinner Nathan Lyon has been left out of Australia's squad for the four-test series against New Zealand, with selectors opting for uncapped Western Australia spinner Corey Rocchiccioli. Lyon's omission casts doubt over the international future of the 39-year-old offspinner, Australia's second highest wicket-taker in tests, behind only Shane Warne. “Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches,” selectors boss George Bailey said in a statement on Saturday. “We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward.”

WASHINGTON, Nov 27 : The internet bandwidth provider RETN is being barred from US networks, the US government said in a notice posted to the Federal Register on Friday. Here are some more details: • The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in the notice RETN poses "undue and unacceptable risks" identified in a 2019 executive order about hostile foreign IT firms. • The notice said RETN and its successors must "decommission and remove all equipment it has provided or installed either directly or through third parties from any U.S. network, and terminate services provided to U.S. persons" effective January 1, 2027.

LONDON, Nov 27 : James McNabney scored two tries as Ireland secured fifth place in the inaugural Nations Championship with a clinical 38-14 victory over Australia at Twickenham on Friday. Australia dominated possession and territory, but stout Irish defence and costly errors restricted them to two tries and left them feeling that, despite the one-sided scoreline, this was a match that got away. Ireland also crossed for tries through centre Robbie Henshaw, number eight Nick Timoney and winger Rob Baloucoune, but spent much of the contest in their own half. Australia attacked with ball in hand and had plenty of entries into the Ireland 22, and will be disappointed they could only manage scores via lock Jeremy Williams and scrumhalf Kalani Thomas.

"We stuck with it pretty well, there were some scrappy parts there but we were clinical at times, especially towards the end,” Ireland flyhalf Sam Prendergast said. "We showed good composure at times but there is a lot we can be better at. But we have won four from four (games in November) which is something we wanted.” Australia had 60 per cent possession and territory in front of a sparse crowd in London and did a good job of disrupting the Ireland set-piece, but were left frustrated by sloppy play at crucial moments. After no points in the opening 21 minutes, Australia finally burrowed their way over when Williams scored from close range, but Ireland hit back with a simple backline move to get Henshaw over near the posts. Australia continued to see much of the ball but their inaccuracy will be frustrating for coach Les Kiss. By contrast Ireland made their entries into the 22 count as they scored a second try from a driving maul through Timoney. Ireland’s efficiency was on display again early in the second half as they moved the ball through the phases and when debutant Australia wing James Ramm failed to collect a cross-kick from Prendergast, Baloucoune had an easy run-in to score. Australia were camped in the Ireland 22 but it took them almost 15 minutes of the second half to score their second try as Thomas crossed. It was ‘game on’ then but Ireland scored twice late on through McNabney's double to put a gloss on the scoreline.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NOTTINGHAM, Nov 27 : Chelsea suffered a third successive Premier League defeat as Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice for Nottingham Forest in a 3-2 victory at a cold and rainy City Ground on Friday. A stunning volley by Igor Jesus gave Forest a fifth-minute lead and Gibbs-White made it 2-0 from the penalty spot six minutes after the interval after Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana had clumsily brought down ex Chelsea player Liam Delap. Substitute Emmanuel Emegha pulled a goal back almost immediately for the visitors but Gibbs-White was played in by a superb dinked pass by Xaver Schlager to restore his side's two-goal advantage after 72 minutes. There were late nerves for the hosts though as Emegha struck again with a header from Pedro Neto's cross in the 89th minute but Forest hung on for a first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997.

Defeat increased the scrutiny on Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, whose side have now lost four of their last five league games and sit eighth in the table. Forest moved up to 14th place. "It's a difficult moment for everyone, for the fans, for sure it's disappointing to lose again," Alonso told Sky Sports. "We need to keep trying to find solutions, trying to be critical, we can't stop. We are low in confidence but we are responsible to try and find solutions. "We can do better for sure." Chelsea have now conceded 23 Premier League goals in 12 games, a total only surpassed by bottom club Crystal Palace who Chelsea face at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday. Another bad result then and the pressure will really start to mount on former Liverpool midfielder Alonso but for Forest's new manager Oliver Glasner, things are looking up. They have now beaten Manchester City and Chelsea in their last three games and appear to be getting to grips with former Palace boss Glasner's demands. "I feel we need to take a bit of realisation that we have a new manager, we're sticking with him, we're trusting the process, believing in him and trusting what he wants," Gibbs-White said. "Not every week is it going to be pretty or is it going to be nice, but when times like this happen tonight we've got to make the most of it and enjoy it."

Source: Reuters

DUBAI: The US military said on Friday (Nov 27) it disabled a commercial ship that attempted to run the US blockade of Iran, while an adviser to Iran' supreme leader said T ehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut and vowed to break the US embargo . US Central Command said in a statement that military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it departed from the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas. The ship’s propulsion was disabled while the civilian crew was unharmed, Central Command said. The US reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports in July, and earlier this month announced Task Force Iron Gate to restrict the movement of weapons and sanctioned materials across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, vowed on Friday to break the embargo, according to Iranian state media. "Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place," state media reported Mokhber saying. He did not give details of Iran's plans for breaking the embargo. Separately, Iranian navy commander Shahram Irani told state television: "Breaking through the enemy blockade is underway and our ports are active today. Contrary to all propaganda, maritime escorts are taking place and we stand with the shipowners and sailors." "The enemy's attempt is to cut off the lifeblood of our economy in whatever way it can, and this has so far failed," Irani said, without giving details.

LONDON, Nov 27 : Fullback Tommaso Allan kicked a penalty 13 minutes from the end as Italy avoided the wooden spoon in the inaugural Nations Championship with a 23-21 victory over Fiji in their 11th-place playoff at Twickenham on Friday. It was a first win in the competition for the Italians, who lost all six pool games, including a 21-16 defeat by Fiji in Udine last weekend, and will come as a relief to coach Gonzalo Quesada who has had to deal with a slew of injuries. Fiji had their chances to win and will rue a slow start, but there were more signs of improvement under new coach Jake White. "It was physical, fair play to Fiji," Italy's South African-born flanker Ross Vintcent said. "We wanted to end this tournament on a high. We owed it to ourselves, the staff and everyone who has supported us.

Nov 27 : OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices, after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology. The ChatGPT maker filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple's employment practices were designed to "trap" employees and prevent them from working on competitors' technology.  OpenAI is developing AI-enabled personal electronic devices that threaten to "outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf," the company said in its Friday court filing. OpenAI said in the filing that Apple gained confidential information by rehiring a former employee who worked at OpenAI for six months. In that time, the employee gained access to specific information on a new device as well as OpenAI's roadmap for future hardware products.

"[G]iven the timing, it now appears that stealing those documents may have been his reason for joining OpenAI in the first place," OpenAI said. Apple denied using the rehired employee to access OpenAI's confidential information and denied trying to suppress competition in AI device manufacturing. "OpenAI’s counterclaims are a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple’s lawsuit," Apple said in a Friday statement. Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology. Apple sued OpenAI and former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu in July, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner's foray into consumer hardware. Tan, a 24-year Apple employee who was a vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch, was part of the group that launched the AI device startup io Products before it was acquired by OpenAI in 2025. OpenAI and the employees have denied those allegations and said that Apple's lawsuit depended on its unauthorized monitoring of Liu's personal messages after he stopped working for Apple. OpenAI and attorneys for Tan and Liu did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday's court filing. In Friday's filing, OpenAI criticized Apple for encouraging employees to do work on their personal Apple devices and accounts, then preventing those employees from an orderly separation of work and personal accounts when they leave for new jobs. OpenAI said that Apple continues to access former employees' personal devices and accounts after they leave the company, enabling Apple to "monitor and ensnare departing employees" when they leave for competitors. OpenAI said that 400 employees have left Apple for OpenAI so far, and Apple wants to intimidate other employees from leaving to find other tech companies.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NAIROBI: A Kenyan court found starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of manslaughter on Friday (Nov 27) for the deaths of 123 of his followers, the latest conviction over one of the deadliest cult-related massacres in modern times. Mackenzie , already serving a 200-year jail sentence from earlier this month for the murder of nearly 200 children, has also been convicted of child cruelty, assault, radicalisation and terrorism-related offences. The preacher led an apocalyptic Christian church in a forest near Kenya's Indian Ocean coast, telling his followers to starve themselves and their children to death to reach heaven before the end of the world. His suspected 500 victims included children buried alive or dumped in latrines.

Delivering his judgement in a court in the city of Mombasa, magistrate Alex Ithuku said Mackenzie "gave the directions to fast to death ... the order in which people were to die, directed the faithful move to secluded fasting places, and took part in what followed these deaths". Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty to manslaughter, and one of his lawyers said he would appeal it after sentencing. The scale of the killings in the Shakahola Forest, which gradually emerged from April 2023 onwards, has shocked Kenya and prompted calls for tighter oversight of religious groups. In 2023, President William Ruto said he took responsibility as head of state for the government's failure to prevent the deaths. Comparable mass killings include a doomsday cult that killed more than 700 people in Uganda in 2000 and a 1978 massacre in Guyana, where an American cult leader killed over 900 people by ordering them to drink poison.

Source: Reuters/fs

Nov 27 : Audi have lost an appeal over the Italian Formula One Grand Prix last September that might have gained them a point for 10th place. The governing FIA said in a statement on Friday that the appeal, while admissible, had been dismissed and the original stewards' decision upheld after a hearing in Paris on Wednesday. Yuki Tsunoda finished 10th for Racing Bulls at Monza after stewards decided to take no further action over an extra formation lap triggered by the Japanese driver's placing of the car on the grid at a race restart. A driver who causes an extra formation lap would normally have to go around and start from the pitlane, facing a mandatory stop-and-go penalty if he failed to do so, but the Japanese driver continued as normal and received no sanction.

LONDON, Nov 27 : Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has challenged his players to maintain the mindset that has seen them set a new club record of 10 successive victories in all competitions. After a tricky start to life as Andoni Iraola's successor, Rose has masterminded an astonishing run of form that has put them fifth in the Premier League and top of the Europa League. They showed plenty of grit as they battled back from a goal down and being down to 10 men on Thursday to win at Celta Vigo and face Fulham away on Sunday. "Of course, it feels good because we have a run like we have and we should continue like this," the German said.

Bournemouth are the seventh Premier League club since 2000 to win 10 successive games in all competitions, and victory at Fulham would mean only Manchester City and Arsenal have managed longer runs in the Premier League era. BOLOGNA, Italy, Nov 27 : Defending champions Italy survived another cliff-hanger to reach the Davis Cup final as Lorenzo Musetti and Andrea Vavassori won the deciding doubles to clinch a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic in Bologna on Friday. After the singles rubbers were shared, Musetti and Vavassori went a set down against Jiri Lehecka and Tomas Machac. But roared on by a partisan crowd, they hit back for a 3-6 6-1 7-6(4) win. Italy, who have now won 16 successive ties dating back to 2023, will aim for a fourth consecutive title against either Spain or Britain on Sunday. They play their semi on Saturday. The Czechs looked on course to reach their first final since 2013 when they took the opening set of the doubles thanks to a single service break secured when Vavassori blazed a smash wildly over the baseline.

Italy seized the momentum in the second set though to send the tie down to a one-set shoot-out. The Czech duo had a break point for a 5-3 lead but could not convert it and also led in the tiebreak. But Italy, who are without world number two Jannik Sinner, simply would not be denied and Musetti smashed away a winner on match point to spark wild celebrations on the court and in the stands. "This has a special meaning in my heart," a hoarse Musetti said on court with Vavassori. "My last matches in Davis Cup weren't a win, so I felt like I needed this, to come back and prove that I could help the team. "I don't have a voice because I screamed all the match, but I'm really happy and proud of that we did." Italy had also needed the final doubles rubber to edge past South Korea in the quarter-finals on Wednesday. Musetti, who returned to Davis Cup action for the first time since 2024 this week, had put Italy ahead with an assured 6-3 6-4 defeat of Jakub Mensik in the opening singles. But the powerful Lehecka squared it up for the Czechs when he beat world number seven Flavio Cobolli 6-2 1-6 6-3. Italy captain Filippo Volandri then opted to send out Musetti, rather than Matteo Berrettini, alongside doubles specialist Vavassori and the gamble paid off. Should Italy win the title again they would be the first nation to win the men's team event four times in a row since the United States in the early 1970s.

Source: Reuters

Nov 27 : Agit Kabayel was handed the WBC heavyweight world title by email last June but the German plans to show the world what he is really made of on Saturday. The 34-year-old became champion when Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk relinquished the belt and the WBC promoted the fighter of Kurdish origin to title holder.    "I was on a plane on my way to Mallorca. After landing, my phone felt like it exploded. My manager then told me it was me. I just asked him: What am I? He said: You're the world champion," Kabayel recalled this week.  The former security guard son of refugees is overwhelming favourite in his first defence, against unbeaten Albanian Nelson Hysa at Duesseldorf's 60,000-capacity Merkur Spiel Arena.

He is Germany's first heavyweight champion since Max Schmeling in 1932. “People tell me I’m the email champion, but now we will show the world I’m not the email champion,” Kabayel told broadcaster DAZN this week. The champion should draw a big crowd but still feels he deserves more recognition at home.   “When our footballers become world champions or German athletes win a medal at the Olympics, they are honoured by the Federal President, or the Federal Chancellor might give them a call. When I became world champion, no politician was interested except for the mayor of my hometown of Bochum,” he told Bild and Die Welt this week. Kabayel, with an unbeaten 27-0 record, weighed in on Friday at 235.7 pounds versus Hysa's 249.3. Both men are managed by British promoter Frank Warren's Queensberry Promotions, with 42-year-old Hysa - fighting on Albanian independence weekend - 16th in the latest WBC rankings with a 25-0 record. The stadium, home to soccer team Fortuna Duesseldorf, was where British heavyweight Tyson Fury, an old sparring partner of Kabayel, beat Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to take the WBA, IBF, WBO and IBO titles. Saturday's fight will mean all of the titles relinquished by Usyk have now been fought for, with Britain's Daniel Dubois holding the WBO belt and Croatia's Filip Hrgovic in possession of the IBF one. Russian Murat Gassievis the WBA champion.

Source: Reuters
